title: Training Notes: Repeat Billing Errors on One Wayfare Rides Trip
content:
**The rule.** When a fare charge on **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)** was billed above the guaranteed fare, the repeat-error multiplier applied to the billing-error make-good counts the refund and fare adjustment entries support had already booked on the same trip before this correction: two or more such entries take the two-error multiplier of 2.0, exactly one takes the one-error multiplier of 1.5, and with none the repeat-error multiplier is not raised.

| Refund and fare adjustment entries already booked on the trip | Repeat-error multiplier |
|---|---|
| none | not raised |
| exactly one | 1.5 |
| two or more | 2.0 |

## Questions the rule answers

**Which entries count?** Every refund entry and every fare adjustment entry already booked on the same trip before this correction, whatever charge of the trip it was booked against and whatever its reason.

**Does a refund of the trip's toll count the same as an adjustment of its fare?** Yes; both are entries already booked on the trip, and each counts once.

**Do entries on the rider's other trips count?** No; only the same trip is counted.

**Does a waiver entry count?** No; only refund and fare adjustment entries are counted.

## Example (hypothetical)

A trip already carries one fare adjustment for wait time not incurred and one refund of a toll not incurred. That is two entries, so the multiplier is 2.0.
